fields.description: Issue dated February 9, 1935 (Vol. 9, No. 21). Prominent coverage includes commentary on Dade County grand jury indictments and allegations of corruption involving public safety and police officials, with discussion of bribery and the absence of indictments for bribe payers. Features an open letter to Postmaster General James A. Farley criticizing his stay at the Miami Biltmore Hotel operated by Henry L. Doherty amid federal scrutiny of holding-company practices. Includes local columns and letters on Miami Beach gambling enforcement, a Torch K-9 Club response, an explanation of the National Housing Act by FHA district director Frank C. Hilson, and extensive racing/gambling tips and advertisements tied to Hialeah Park.
